body:
Because the logic for fully-generic, templated functions have to be declared in a header *somewhere*. This is the only way (to my knowledge) to define forward declared logic between two separate files *without* requiring an entirely separate header include.

A more practical use-case would be applying this logic to `constexpr` structs, as that would allow them to fully interop in `constexpr` contexts. So something like a sanity check, `static_assert(Vector2(0, 0) == Vector2i(0, 0))`, could be included in that file outright to make sure everything is properly synced

body:
Ah, so it does! So this technique actually isn't necessary with generic templates. I was applying it out of habit because this *is* required for fully-declared types; so `Vector2`/`Vector2i` would use this if they became `constexpr`.

That thankfully simplifies matters greatly, but means my initial writeup isn't necessary anymore, oops. Gonna reuse that for some `constexpr` math PR I'll inevitably cook up in the future.

Setup some tests for these new constructors, and attempting to change to `T *` results in this error:
```
D:\Godot\Github\godot\core/variant/typed_array.h(74): error C2440: 'initializing': cannot convert from 'const T' to 'const T *&'
        with
        [
            T=Object *
        ]
        and
        [
            T=Object
        ]
D:\Godot\Github\godot\core/variant/typed_array.h(74): note: Conversion loses qualifiers
D:\Godot\Github\godot\core/variant/typed_array.h(74): note: the template instantiation context (the oldest one first) is
D:\Godot\Github\godot\tests/core/variant/test_array.h(665): note: see reference to class template instantiation 'TypedArray<Object>' being compiled
D:\Godot\Github\godot\core/variant/typed_array.h(71): note: while compiling class template member function 'TypedArray<Object>::TypedArray(const List<T *,DefaultAllocator> &)'
        with
        [
            T=Object
        ]
D:\Godot\Github\godot\tests/core/variant/test_array.h(709): note: see the first reference to 'TypedArray<Object>::TypedArray' in 'TestArray::DOCTEST_ANON_FUNC_5928'
```
I *think* it's interpreting `T`'s pointer as part of the type declaration for the element itself, rather than keeping them isolated. `std::add_pointer_t<T>` seems to avoid this, so I'm sticking with it.

If I'm not mistaken, you're declaring the function here but defining it in the `TypedArray` header? I'm not sure that's needed, as mentioned before the forward declaration should suffice to have directly define the function here, I think. It should only fail if the full type is not known by the time of the call.

I'm guessing you added the add / remove pointer functions because such behavior exists a few times in the codebase?
I'm not sure we want to encourage and abstract this behavior by adding helper functions. People may use it when it's inappropriate, or worse without understanding what it's actually doing (referencing into the other array), which could lead to bugs.
I would prefer if we didn't add helper functions for this, such that callers have it 'harder' and have to manually reference and dereference objects.
